newsitem.title: USA: Comcast, Md. college in broadband deal.
newsitem.headline: Comcast, Md. college in broadband deal.

text.p: Comcast Cablevision of Maryland LP said Monday it agreed to a deal with Towson State University to wire the university to gives students some of the fastest residential Internet access in the nation.
The high-speed Internet service, called ComcastTowson State University, will be provided to 1,700 residential and dormitory rooms throughout Towson State University serving more than 3,000 students.
The Internet service uses Comcast's hybrid fiber optical coaxail (HFC) network, Towson State's HFC Network and Motorola Inc cable modems to provide the student service.
The deal makes Towson State one of the first U.S. higher education institutions to offer a high-speed Internet service for use in student residences.
The deal has received the backing of the Maryland State Board of Public Works. The pact calls for all 1,700 residential locations to be wired with the Comcast Internet service by late May 1997.
